svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 8 components · 21 data flows · 8 trust boundaries (1 inferred) · 81 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-03; tb-2 External → C-09; tb-4 External → C-04; tb-7 C-03 → External; tb-9 C-04 → External
Trust boundary crossing: tb-5 C-03 → C-05; tb-6 C-01 → C-07
df-001: Chatbot model requests via OpenAI-compatible provider client (HTTP) df-002: Startup model availability check GET {llmApiUrl}/models (HTTP)
df-003: POST of solved-challenge notification including CTF flag and host details to configured webhook (HTTP)
df-004: Server-side fetch of requester-supplied profile image URL (HTTP)
df-005: WebSocket RPC subscription to NFTMinted contract events (WebSocket) df-006: WebSocket RPC subscription to ContractExploited contract events (WebSocket)

df-007: Sequelize ORM access to SQLite file data/juiceshop.sqlite · SQLite (in-process) df-007 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-008: In-process MarsDB collections for reviews (posts) and orders · MarsDB (in-process) df-008 authentication: Embedded MarsDB engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9, data/mongodb.ts:10

df-010: OAuth authorization (HTTPS) df-010 authentication: The identity provider authenticates the user at its sign-in endpoint; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148
df-011: OAuth profile request (HTTPS) df-011 authentication: The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68

df-012: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-012 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52, routes/orderHistory.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:156
df-013: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP) df-014: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP)

df-016: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-016 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:178, lib/insecurity.ts:52 df-016 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-017: API requests (other) (HTTP) df-017 authentication: the handler checks the supplied TOTP code against the account secret and rejects an invalid code; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:31 df-017 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-018: API requests (password) (HTTP) df-018 authentication: the handler checks the supplied password and rejects the request without a valid one; evidence: routes/login.ts:34 df-018 access group: API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-020: Direct requests (cookie) (HTTP) df-020 authentication: the handler checks a cookie credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: routes/profileImageFileUpload.ts:35, routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:21, routes/userProfile.ts:34, routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17, routes/dataErasure.ts:26, routes/dataErasure.ts:76
Internet Attacker → C-03 · Juice Shop Express API: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7
Internet Attacker → C-09 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 1, 2, 4, 5; its findings also affect C-01 · Sequelize application data access
Internet Attacker → C-04 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 4, 5; its findings also affect C-09 · Authentication & Session Surface
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: lib/xml.ts:12, lib/xml.ts:38, routes/b2bOrder.ts:23, routes/captcha.ts:22

Further capabilities: WebSocket endpoint — evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:20, lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23; Blockchain client — evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:18, routes/web3Wallet.ts:20
C-03 · Juice Shop Express API: LLM and Alchemy service API keys
C-05 · marsdb Embedded Store: Product reviews and orders
C-07 · SQLite Embedded Store: Application records in SQLite
C-07 · SQLite Embedded Store: User credentials and session tokens
OpenAI-compatible model endpoint selected by the application.chatBot.llmApiUrl setting; used by the chatbot and queried for /models availability.
Fixed-host WebSocket RPC provider eth-sepolia.g.alchemy.com used to listen for contract events.
Destination chosen by the SOLUTIONS_WEBHOOK setting; receives a JSON notification when a challenge is solved.
Arbitrary URL supplied by a logged-in requester in imageUrl; the server fetches it.

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
trust change within a column (dashed: inferred)
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
